title: 721 AMXS Fall Rescue Plan
description: Training video for the 721st Aircraft Maintenance Squadron's Fall Rescue Plan. Covers process of rescuing personnel who have fallen from a wing or T-tail while waiting for first responders.
keywords: prevention, plan, squadron, Fall, States, AMXS, frp, 721st, FPP, MX, 721, aircraft, maintenance, rescue, military, Force, air, united

transcript.text: - I'm Tech Sergeant Jamir Dominguez here from the
721st AMXS stationed at Ramstein Air Base.
As we all know, fall protection is a big deal
in the Air Force.
But here at Ramstein Air Base, we have a unique situation
where the ladder truck is stationed in Landstuhl
about 20 minutes away and if somebody's dangling
from the wing or the t-tail, you have to be able to recover
that person in less than six minutes
before permanent bodily damage occurs.
(clock ticking slowly)
We've made our own recovery plan, how to rescue
an individual in case he or she falls
off the wing or t-tail.
Before maintainer goes on top of the wing or the t-tail,
the ground observer will call Mach and inform them
there's an individual on top of the wing or tail.
- Mach, hanger five.
Show one each individual on the wing at this time.
- In the event that that member falls,
the ground observer will contact mach
and request fire department assistance
as well as notifying that an individual
has fallen off the wing or tail.
- Mach, hanger five.
Requesting fire department assistance.
One each individual fell off the wing.
- At this time, the ground observer will wheel the stand
to rescue the member, if the member has fallen off the wing
or operate the pre-position condor
if they're working on the tail.
If the member has fallen off the wing, the ground observer
after he has pushed the stand up,
he will release the lanyard from the harness
and lower the stand down and perform SABC.
If the member has fallen off the tail,
the basket operator of the condor will attach
the extra lanyard already attached to the basket
to the member and then remove the lanyard
that's attached to the airplane
and lower the member to the ground.
Once on the ground, he or she will perform SABC
until fire department arrives.
So our policy here is no matter what operation
you're gonna do, you always need a ground observer.
If you're going to access the top of the wing,
you need a B7 stand or a B5.
If you're going to access the t-tail,
you need to have a condor already set up
with a ground guy and an operator for the basket
and an extra lanyard.
Here at the 721st AMXS, our whole goal is to familiarize
and expose all our airmen to the fall protection program
that we have in place as well as how to act
and perform with the fall recovery plan
that we have in motion already.
The point of all this is to make sure
that everybody goes home safely.
